scope: Ten diagnostic replays of recorded cases, twenty fixed-clock samples; not a new policy or strength trial. Approach-covered means grounded and approach cover, with departure and low-altitude exceptions recorded separately in raw observations. Unmeasured sites, future cover and physical execution remain unknown.

findings: All 37 approach-covered observed sites in the directed failure have disconnected outbound routes; two newly measured usable sites are also exposed.
The successful control already has four native eligible covered alternatives; extra survey breadth is unnecessary for its successful selection.
The recorded asteroid case contains a covered native route that loses on score, followed by 17 covered round trips omitted from the native shortlist.
All 11 approach-covered sites in the neutral asteroid snapshot are rejected on solar safety in both directions.
The first cooldown exclusion in each changed fresh match has no approach-covered round trip among all observed sites.
decision.next_experiment: After a witnessed cover failure, distinguish a known eligible covered route from unmeasured alternatives and currently blocked approaches. Test a cover requirement with bounded evidence acquisition and an explicit exit when the approach cannot progress. Preserve solar/route gates, unexposed initial choices, deadlines and work quotas.
decision.limitations: Known diagnostic snapshots and modeled routes only. No strength, future-cover, completed-execution or Pi performance claim. Missing native route evidence does not prove impossibility.
